es: Comprender un debate público: identificar quién decide, quién se beneficia y cuál es la razón de una norma, distinguir intención de impacto y reconocer lo que se encarga a terceros (have + objeto + participio).

teaching.en: The council decides the rules, but residents are the ones who live with them every day, and they rarely have a real say in the outcome.
teaching.es: El municipio decide las normas, pero los vecinos son quienes viven con ellas cada día, y rara vez tienen voz real en el resultado.
teaching.explanationEs: Quien decide y quien soporta la decisión son papeles distintos. Have a say: tener voz en una decisión.
segments: The council decides the rules, but residents are the ones who live with
them every day, and they rarely have a real say in the outcome.
teaching.audioText: The council decides the rules, but residents are the ones who live with them every day, and they rarely have a real say in the outcome.

teaching.en: Shop owners, parents and cyclists are all stakeholders in the new traffic plan, and several of them have a vested interest, because the outcome will affect their income.
teaching.es: Comerciantes, padres y ciclistas son partes interesadas en el nuevo plan de tráfico, y varios tienen un interés personal, porque el resultado afectará a sus ingresos.
teaching.explanationEs: Stakeholder: quien se ve afectado por una decisión aunque no la tome. Vested interest: interés propio, a menudo económico.
segments: Shop owners, parents and cyclists are all stakeholders in the new traffic plan, and
several of them have a vested interest, because the outcome will affect their income.
teaching.audioText: Shop owners, parents and cyclists are all stakeholders in the new traffic plan, and several of them have a vested interest, because the outcome will affect their income.

teaching.en: Who will benefit from the new rule, and who will pay for it? A good debate always asks both questions before anyone votes.
teaching.es: ¿Quién se beneficiará de la nueva norma y quién la pagará? Un buen debate siempre plantea ambas preguntas antes de votar.
teaching.explanationEs: Benefit from + norma: quien gana. Se contrasta con who pays, que señala a quien soporta el coste.
segments: Who will benefit from the new rule, and who will pay for
it? A good debate always asks both questions before anyone votes.
teaching.audioText: Who will benefit from the new rule, and who will pay for it? A good debate always asks both questions before anyone votes.

teaching.en: The rationale is simple: fewer cars mean safer streets near the school, although a rule that helps some people may come at the expense of others.
teaching.es: La razón de fondo es sencilla: menos autos significan calles más seguras cerca del colegio, aunque una norma que ayuda a unos puede ir a costa de otros.
teaching.explanationEs: Rationale: la razón que justifica la norma. At the expense of + personas o cosas: perjudicándolas para beneficiar a otros.
segments: The rationale is simple: fewer cars mean safer streets near the school, although
a rule that helps some people may come at the expense of others.
teaching.audioText: The rationale is simple: fewer cars mean safer streets near the school, although a rule that helps some people may come at the expense of others.

teaching.en: The council argues that the ban is intended to protect children, but its impact on small shops could be serious; an unintended consequence is an effect nobody planned.
teaching.es: El municipio sostiene que la prohibición pretende proteger a los niños, pero su impacto en los comercios podría ser serio; una consecuencia no prevista es un efecto que nadie había planeado.
teaching.explanationEs: Intended to = la intención; impact = el efecto real, que puede ser distinto. Unintended consequence: lo que pasa sin que nadie lo buscara.
segments: The council argues that the ban is intended to protect children, but its impact
on small shops could be serious; an unintended consequence is an effect nobody planned.
teaching.audioText: The council argues that the ban is intended to protect children, but its impact on small shops could be serious; an unintended consequence is an effect nobody planned.

teaching.en: The council has the old bus shelter repaired by a contractor, which means it pays for the work but does not do it.
teaching.es: El municipio hace reparar la vieja parada de autobús a un contratista, lo que significa que paga el trabajo pero no lo hace.
teaching.explanationEs: Have + objeto + participio: encargas el trabajo a otro; tú no lo haces. Contractor: empresa o persona contratada.
segments: The council has the old bus shelter repaired by a contractor, which
means it pays for the work but does not do it.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige quién toma la decisión.

choices.text: The council.
The residents.
The shop owners.

feedback.es: El verbo voted y el sujeto the council indican quién decide; vecinos y comerciantes solo hablaron en la reunión.

hint.es: El decisor es quien vota o aprueba la norma, no quien habla en la reunión.

origin.audio: The council voted last night to close Mill Street to cars during school hours. Residents and shop owners both spoke at the meeting, but only the council members took the vote.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿quién se beneficia de la norma?

choices.text: Shop owners, because they will sell more.
Parents, because the streets will be safer.
The council, because it will earn money.

feedback.es: Los padres ganan calles más seguras; los comerciantes temen un impacto negativo y el municipio habla de seguridad, no de beneficios.

hint.es: Busca el grupo que recibe un efecto positivo.

origin.text: Parents welcome the ban because fewer cars mean safer streets near the school. Shop owners fear the impact on their sales, and the council says the rationale is safety, not profit.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Quién se beneficiará de esta norma y quién la pagará?»

feedback.es: Benefit from + norma señala a quien gana con ella; se contrasta con quien paga.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa «beneficiarse» y va con from.

origin.text: Every new rule helps some people and costs others. Who will ___ from this one, and who will pay for it?

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige qué objeción plantea el vecino.

choices.text: That customers can no longer park near his shop.
That the results of the study will not be published.
That nobody asked the people on the street.

feedback.es: El vecino dice que nadie preguntó a quienes viven en la calle; el comercio teme por el estacionamiento y el contratista solo estudia el tráfico.

origin.audio: At a public meeting, the council's spokesperson explained the plan. The rationale, she said, is simple: the bus lane is intended to cut journey times, so commuters will benefit most. Then a shop owner spoke. He agreed with the aim, but argued that parking is how his customers reach him, so the impact on his business would be serious. A resident added that nobody had asked the people who live on the street. The spokesperson replied that the council had chosen a contractor to study the traffic, and that the results would be published before the final vote.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión del debate con su significado.

feedback.es: El contractor ejecuta un encargo, los stakeholders son los afectados, un vested interest es un interés propio y una unintended consequence no estaba prevista.

prompt.es: Lee el artículo: ¿qué quiere ilustrar el autor con el ejemplo?

choices.text: That intention and impact can differ greatly.
That litter bans never work in any city.
That the mayor ignored the complaints from the start.

feedback.es: El alcalde buscaba reducir la basura, pero el problema se trasladó a otras calles: la intención y el impacto no coinciden.

origin.text: The mayor insists that the ban is intended to reduce litter, but after three months complaints have doubled, because people now leave rubbish in the side streets. Nobody wanted that outcome. It shows how a rule can work on paper and go wrong in practice, and why the people affected should be heard before, not after.

prompt.es: Escucha a la vecina y elige quién saldría ganando con la tasa de estacionamiento.

choices.text: Local workers and their families.
People who drive into town from outside.
Shop owners in the town centre.

feedback.es: La vecina dice que quienes vienen en auto a la ciudad se beneficiarían de calles más vacías, mientras que los trabajadores del barrio pagarían.

origin.audio: Ms Park, a resident, spoke for two minutes at the council. She said she was not against the new parking charge in principle; what worried her was who would pay. Drivers who come into town would benefit from emptier streets, she said, but the workers who live nearby would pay, at the expense of their own family budgets. She asked the council to show the evidence for its rationale before the vote. The mayor thanked her, but did not promise any change.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué actitud muestra la vecina hacia la norma?

choices.text: She welcomes the charge but trusts the council to be fair.
She doubts the charge will change how people drive.
She accepts the idea but asks who pays.

feedback.es: No está en contra de la tasa en principio («not against»), pero cuestiona quién la paga y pide pruebas: acepta la idea y critica el reparto del coste.

origin.audio: Ms Park, a resident, spoke for two minutes at the council. She said she was not against the new parking charge in principle; what worried her was who would pay. Drivers who come into town would benefit from emptier streets, she said, but the workers who live nearby would pay, at the expense of their own family budgets. She asked the council to show the evidence for its rationale before the vote. The mayor thanked her, but did not promise any change.

prompt.es: Completa: «El municipio no pinta los bancos; hace que los pinte un contratista.»

feedback.es: Have + objeto + participio (painted) expresa que el trabajo lo hace otro.

origin.text: The council does not paint the benches itself. It has the benches ___ by a contractor every spring.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los comerciantes sostienen que el impacto será serio.»

answer.text: Shop owners argue that the impact will be serious

feedback.es: Argue that + oración introduce la postura de un grupo; impact es el efecto real de la norma.

prompt.es: Escucha la entrevista: ¿qué reconoce la representante del municipio?

choices.text: That the rule had an effect nobody expected.
That the rule was a mistake from the start.
That the shops closed for reasons unrelated to the ban.

feedback.es: Admite que nadie había previsto el cierre de las tiendas: una consecuencia no prevista, y promete revisar la norma.

origin.audio: In a radio interview, a council member defended the ban on cars near the school. The intention, she said, was never to hurt shops, but to protect children at the school gates. When the interviewer pointed out that two shops had already closed, she admitted that nobody had predicted that effect, and promised a review within six months.

prompt.es: Lee la carta: ¿con qué propósito la escribe el vecino?

choices.text: To ask the council to cancel the contractor's project.
To demand a say before any decision.
To explain why residents are happy to be called stakeholders.

feedback.es: Se queja de que los vecinos se enteran después y pide hablar con los afectados antes de decidir.

origin.text: I have lived on this street for thirty years, and I am tired of hearing that we are all stakeholders. The council decides, the contractor builds, and residents are told afterwards. If the rationale is good, it will not be afraid of a conversation with the people who live here.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quien posee los locales tiene un interés personal en la norma.»

feedback.es: Vested interest es el interés propio, normalmente económico, que alguien tiene en un resultado; aquí falta el sustantivo.

origin.text: A landlord who owns several shops on the street has a vested ___ in how the rule turns out.
